Progress in worktree ../release-0.13.1 (branch release-0.13.1 off origin/main @ 27cdc312846a):
- pyproject.toml, server.json (both version fields), uv.lock bumped to 0.13.1.
- CHANGELOG.md: generated the [0.13.1] section via make changelog, hand-curated into Fixed (MCP registry description-length guard, prompt-cache-follows-primary fallback fix) and Ops (SSM write-only migration, module-size splits, enrichment self-heal debounce) sections; fresh empty Unreleased section and updated compare links added.
- Reinstalled the editable package (uv pip install -e . --no-deps) so rebar.__version__ picked up 0.13.1, then regenerated tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json (single-line __version__ diff).
- python scripts/release_guards.py version-lockstep --version 0.13.1 ... exits 0.
- uv lock --check exits 0.
- pytest tests/unit/test_release_guards.py tests/unit/test_release_workflow_pins.py -- 44 passed.
- make lint exits 0. make typecheck exits 0 (694 files).
- make test (full suite): first run hit 8 failures, all in tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py, tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py, and tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py -- confirmed environmental (this session's shell injects GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository/etc, which breaks 'git -C <bare-repo>' in these tests' fixtures), matching the same root cause documented on the 0.13.0 release ticket. Re-ran the 8 with those GIT_CONFIG_* vars unset -- 35 passed. Re-ran the full suite with them unset: 18056 passed, 63 skipped, 305 deselected, 0 failed (78m28s).
- python -m build produced nava_rebar-0.13.1.tar.gz and nava_rebar-0.13.1-py3-none-any.whl. python -m twine check dist/* -- PASSED both.

Note: could not independently verify/resolve the navapbc org OAuth-App third-party-access restriction that blocked the 0.13.0 release's manual mcp-publisher fallback (requires org-admin admin:org scope I don't have). Proceeding with the normal single-dispatch release.yml path per the ticket's plan; will fall back to the documented [non-codebase, known-blocked] exception AC if mcp_registry fails again after PyPI publish succeeds.

Next: commit with DCO + rebar-ticket trailer, push to Gerrit.
